mcqs.q: Before the posterior teeth are set, the maxillary anterior teeth are checked for:
mcqs.explain: The maxillary anterior checklist has two items — arch form and symmetry.

mcqs.q: The long axis of the maxillary premolars should be:
opts: Inclined mesially to the occlusal plane
Inclined distally to the occlusal plane
mcqs.explain: The long axis of the premolars should be perpendicular to the occlusal plane.

mcqs.q: Which cusp tips of the maxillary premolars contact the plane of occlusion?
opts: Both the buccal and the palatal cusp tips
mcqs.explain: Both the buccal and lingual (palatal) cusp tips of the maxillary premolars should contact the plane of occlusion.

mcqs.q: On the maxillary FIRST molar, which cusp tip contacts the occlusal plane?
mcqs.explain: The mesio-palatal cusp tip of the 1st molar contacts the occlusal plane.

mcqs.q: On the maxillary first molar, the buccal cusp tips and the distal lingual cusp are elevated off the occlusal plane by approximately:
mcqs.explain: They are elevated about 0.5 mm off the occlusal plane.

mcqs.q: How many cusps of the maxillary SECOND molar touch the occlusal plane?
mcqs.explain: On the maxillary second molar, no cusps touch the occlusal plane.

mcqs.q: On the maxillary second molar, the mesiopalatal cusp and the buccal cusps stand above the occlusal plane by, respectively:
mcqs.explain: The mesiopalatal cusp is 1.0 mm above the plane and the buccal cusps are 1.5 mm above it.

mcqs.q: Reading the maxillary posterior teeth from the premolars back to the second molar, what is progressively created?
opts: The orientation of the occlusal plane
mcqs.explain: The teeth rise progressively off the plane from front to back and the palatal side stays lower than the buccal — that rise IS the compensating curve, anteroposteriorly and mediolaterally.

mcqs.q: Which is NOT one of the four items on the posterior checklist?
mcqs.explain: The posterior checklist is ridge relationship, arch form, arch symmetry and compensating curve.

mcqs.q: The compensating curve is defined as the curving of the occluding surfaces and incisal edges of artificial teeth in which directions?
mcqs.explain: It is the anteroposterior curving AND the mediolateral curving of the occluding surfaces and incisal edges.

mcqs.q: According to its own definition, the compensating curve exists in order to:
opts: Centre the posterior teeth over the ridge
mcqs.explain: The definition itself states that it is used to develop balanced articulation.

mcqs.q: Christensen's phenomenon is:
opts: The space that occurs between opposing occlusal surfaces during mandibular protrusion
The space between the denture base and the mucosa at rest
The contact of the balancing cusps during lateral excursion
The gap between the anterior teeth in centric occlusion
mcqs.explain: Christensen's phenomenon is the space that occurs between opposing occlusal surfaces during mandibular protrusion.

mcqs.q: Which tooth is described as the KEY TOOTH in occlusion and must be arranged first?
mcqs.explain: The mandibular first molar is the key tooth in occlusion, so it has to be arranged first.

mcqs.q: The key of occlusion is that the mesiobuccal cusp of the upper first molar occludes with:
opts: The mesiobuccal groove of the lower first molar
The distobuccal groove of the lower first molar
The central fossa of the lower first molar
The distal marginal ridge of the lower second premolar
mcqs.explain: The mesiobuccal cusp of the upper first molar occludes with the mesiobuccal groove of the lower first molar.

mcqs.q: When setting the mandibular first molar, its mesial buccal cusp tip should engage the embrasure between:
opts: The maxillary 2nd molar and the tuberosity
mcqs.explain: The mesial buccal cusp tip should engage the embrasure between the 1st molar and 2nd premolar.

mcqs.q: The buccal cusp of the mandibular SECOND premolar should occlude with:
opts: The adjacent marginal ridges of the maxillary 1st and 2nd premolars
The mesial marginal ridge of the maxillary 1st premolar only
The central fossa of the maxillary 2nd premolar
The distal marginal ridge of the maxillary canine
mcqs.explain: It occludes with the adjacent marginal ridges of the maxillary 1st and 2nd premolars.

mcqs.q: The buccal cusp of the mandibular FIRST premolar should engage:
opts: The mesial marginal ridge of the opposing 1st premolar
The distal marginal ridge of the opposing 1st premolar
The embrasure between the two maxillary premolars
The mesiobuccal groove of the maxillary 1st molar
mcqs.explain: The buccal cusp of the mandibular 1st premolar engages the mesial marginal ridge of the opposing 1st premolar.

mcqs.q: The mandibular SECOND molar is placed with its mesiobuccal cusp engaging:
opts: Between the maxillary 1st and 2nd molars, contacting their marginal ridges
Between the maxillary 2nd premolar and 1st molar
In the central fossa of the maxillary 2nd molar
Against the distal marginal ridge of the maxillary 2nd molar only
mcqs.explain: It engages between the maxillary 1st and 2nd molars and contacts their marginal ridges.

mcqs.q: The single principle underlying the whole mandibular posterior set-up is that the mandibular cusp tips are designed to:
opts: Engage the embrasures of the opposing maxillary teeth
Rest in the central fossae of the opposing maxillary teeth
Avoid contact with the maxillary teeth in centric
Contact only the palatal cusps of the maxillary teeth
mcqs.explain: The mandibular cusp tips are designed to engage the embrasures of the opposing maxillary teeth.

mcqs.q: After the mandibular posteriors are set, what must be verified?
opts: That they are centred over the crest of the ridge
That they are set buccal to the crest of the ridge
That they are set lingual to the crest of the ridge
That they contact the retromolar pad
mcqs.explain: Verify that the posterior mandibular teeth are centered over the crest of the ridge.

mcqs.q: Why does a posterior tooth set off the ridge crest cause trouble in a complete denture?
opts: It turns a vertical bite force into a tipping force on a base resting only on mucosa
It prevents the compensating curve from being established
It raises the incisal guide angle
It makes the second molar contact the occlusal plane
mcqs.explain: The denture is a rigid unit on mucosa; an off-centre tooth converts vertical load into a tipping force that unseats the base.

mcqs.q: In complete dentures, which relationship holds?
opts: Centric occlusion is 1 mm anterior to centric relation
Centric relation is 1 mm anterior to centric occlusion
mcqs.explain: Centric occlusion = centric relation in complete dentures.

mcqs.q: In the natural dentition, teeth are retained in the periodontal ligament. In a complete denture, by contrast:
opts: The teeth sit on mobile bases on mucosa
The teeth are retained in an artificial ligament
The teeth are rigidly fixed to bone
The teeth are retained by the buccinator
mcqs.explain: Denture 'dentition' consists of mobile bases on mucosa, against natural teeth retained in the PDL.

mcqs.q: Regarding tooth movement, how does a denture differ from a natural dentition?
opts: Denture teeth move as a unit; natural teeth move independently
Denture teeth move independently; natural teeth move as a unit
mcqs.explain: Denture teeth move as a unit, while natural teeth move independently.

mcqs.q: How do the effects of malocclusion differ between the two?
opts: In a denture it affects the entire base immediately; in natural teeth the effects are not immediate
In a denture the effects are not immediate; in natural teeth they are
mcqs.explain: Malocclusion affects the entire denture base immediately, whereas in the natural dentition the effects are not immediate.

mcqs.q: Non-vertical forces on a complete denture:
opts: Affect all the teeth and are traumatic
Affect only the teeth involved and are well tolerated
Are absorbed by the periodontal ligament
Have no effect because the base is rigid
mcqs.explain: On a denture, non-vertical forces affect all teeth and are traumatic; in a natural dentition they affect only the teeth involved and are usually well tolerated.

mcqs.q: Incising with a complete denture:
opts: Affects all teeth attached to the base
Does not affect the posterior teeth
Is impossible and must be avoided entirely
mcqs.explain: Incising affects all teeth attached to the base, unlike the natural dentition where incising does not affect the posteriors.

mcqs.q: Bilateral balance is:
opts: Often desired in dentures for base stability, but rare in the natural dentition
Rare in dentures but common in the natural dentition
mcqs.explain: Bilateral balance is often desired in dentures for base stability, and is rare in the natural dentition.

mcqs.q: Compared with a natural dentition, the complete denture wearer has:
opts: No sensation at all in the denture-bearing area
mcqs.explain: The natural dentition has tactile sensitivity, while the denture wearer has decreased tactile sense.

mcqs.q: Occlusion is defined as:
opts: The static relationship between the incising or masticating surfaces of the teeth
The static and dynamic contact relationship of those surfaces in function
The path the condyles follow within the temporomandibular joint
The anteroposterior and mediolateral curving of the occluding surfaces
mcqs.explain: Occlusion is the STATIC relationship between the incising or masticating surfaces.

mcqs.q: Articulation is defined as:
opts: The static and dynamic contact relationship of the occlusal surfaces in function
The static relationship of the incising or masticating surfaces alone
The space opening between opposing surfaces during protrusion
The influence of the guide pin and guide table on articulator movement
mcqs.explain: Articulation is the static AND dynamic contact relationship between occlusal surfaces during function.

mcqs.q: What single word distinguishes articulation from occlusion?
opts: Dynamic — articulation includes the movement, occlusion is static only
Static — occlusion includes the movement, articulation is dynamic only
Eccentric — only occlusion includes eccentric positions
mcqs.explain: Occlusion is static only; articulation is static AND dynamic, which is why the goal is called balanced ARTICULATION.

mcqs.q: Balanced articulation is defined as:
opts: Bilateral simultaneous anterior and posterior contact in centric and eccentric positions
Contact on the working side only, in centric position alone
Contact of the posterior teeth only, during protrusion alone
Contact of the anterior teeth only, in every excursion
mcqs.explain: It is the bilateral, simultaneous anterior and posterior occlusal contact of teeth in centric and eccentric positions.

mcqs.q: The purpose of balanced articulation in a complete denture is:
mcqs.explain: Balanced articulation is pursued for stability — a denture contacting on one side only will tip off its seat.

mcqs.q: Bilateral balanced denture occlusion with anatomic posterior teeth aims to give bilateral posterior centric contact, centralized forces, and a balanced occlusion in order to:
mcqs.explain: The stated aim is a balanced occlusion to minimize tipping.

mcqs.q: Which is NOT one of the five factors affecting occlusal balance?
mcqs.explain: The five factors are condylar guidance, incisal guidance, orientation of the occlusal plane, compensating curve and cuspal inclination.

mcqs.q: Condylar guidance is due to:
opts: The path the condyles follow in the TMJ
The inclination of the incisal guide table
The steepness of the cusps selected
The curvature of the occluding surfaces
mcqs.explain: Condylar guidance is due to the path the condyles follow in the TMJ.

mcqs.q: Of the five factors affecting occlusal balance, which one does the patient present you with in a complete denture?
mcqs.explain: In complete dentures, of the five factors, the patient presents you with condylar guidance — the other four are under the operator's control.

mcqs.q: A set-up will not balance in protrusion. Which factor can you NOT alter to correct it?
mcqs.explain: Condylar guidance is fixed and patient-determined; the remaining four factors are the ones the operator adjusts.

mcqs.q: Posterior teeth with a 33-degree cuspal inclination are described as:
mcqs.explain: 33 degrees = anatomic, 20 degrees = semi-anatomic, 0 degrees = non-anatomic.

mcqs.q: Posterior teeth with a 20-degree cuspal inclination are:
mcqs.explain: 20 degrees is the semi-anatomic form.

mcqs.q: Which tooth form is referred to as non-anatomic?
mcqs.explain: 0 degrees is the non-anatomic (flat) tooth form.

mcqs.q: Why is a 0-degree posterior tooth more forgiving of inaccuracy in the other four factors?
opts: It has no cusp to interfere during excursion
It has a steeper compensating curve built into it
It cannot be used with a face-bow transfer
It eliminates the need for a centric relation record
mcqs.explain: The steeper the cusp, the more faithfully the other factors must be set; a flat tooth has no cusp to interfere, at the cost of cutting efficiency and appearance.

mcqs.q: A festoon is defined as:
opts: Carvings in the base material simulating the contours of the natural tissues
The polished surface of the denture base including the teeth
The anteroposterior curving of the occluding surfaces
The thin excess acrylic extending beyond the intended border
mcqs.explain: A festoon is carvings in the denture base material of a denture that simulate the contours of the natural tissues that are being replaced by the denture.

mcqs.q: The clinical procedure of patient visit 4 is the:
mcqs.explain: Visit 4's clinical procedure is the try-in appointment; flasking, deflasking, laboratory remount and finishing and polishing are the laboratory procedures.

mcqs.q: Which is NOT one of the laboratory procedures of visit 4?
mcqs.explain: Teeth arrangement belongs to visit 3; visit 4's laboratory procedures are flasking, deflasking, laboratory remount, and finishing and polishing the denture.

mcqs.q: Which maxillary posterior tooth has exactly ONE cusp tip in contact with the occlusal plane?
mcqs.explain: The first molar contacts the plane at its mesio-palatal cusp alone; the premolars contact with both cusps, and the second molar with none.

mcqs.q: A denture is found to contact only on the working side during lateral excursion. What is the consequence?
opts: The base swings away on the balancing side and the denture is unseated
The compensating curve is automatically corrected
The condylar guidance must be reduced
mcqs.explain: Contact on one side only lets the base tip on the other — which is exactly why bilateral balance is sought for base stability.

saqs.q: Describe the position of the maxillary premolars.
saqs.a: The LONG AXIS of the premolars should be PERPENDICULAR TO THE OCCLUSAL PLANE, and BOTH the BUCCAL and the PALATAL (lingual) CUSP TIPS should CONTACT the occlusal plane.

rows: BOTH the buccal and the palatal (lingual) cusp tips contact the plane

saqs.q: Describe the position of the maxillary first molar relative to the occlusal plane.
saqs.a: The MESIO-PALATAL CUSP TIP of the 1st molar CONTACTS the occlusal plane, but the BUCCAL CUSP TIPS and the DISTAL LINGUAL CUSP are ELEVATED ABOUT 0.5 mm OFF the plane.

head: Cusp
Relation to the occlusal plane
rows: Buccal cusp tips and the distal lingual cusp
elevated about 0.5 mm off the plane

saqs.q: Describe the position of the maxillary second molar relative to the occlusal plane.
saqs.a: NO CUSPS TOUCH THE OCCLUSAL PLANE. The mesiopalatal cusp is 1.0 mm above the plane and the buccal cusps are 1.5 mm above it.

saqs.q: Summarise how the three maxillary posterior units relate to the occlusal plane, and say what the pattern creates.
saqs.a: PREMOLARS — long axis perpendicular, BOTH cusp tips TOUCHING. 1st MOLAR — mesio-palatal cusp CONTACTING, buccal and distal lingual cusps about 0.5 mm ABOVE. 2nd MOLAR — NO cusps touching; mesiopalatal 1.0 mm, buccal 1.5 mm above. Read in sequence, the teeth rise progressively off the plane from front to back while the palatal side stays lower than the buccal — and that rise IS the COMPENSATING CURVE, anteroposteriorly and mediolaterally.

head: Unit
Relation to the occlusal plane
rows: mesio-palatal cusp contacting; buccal and distal lingual cusps about 0.5 mm above
no cusps touching — mesiopalatal 1.0 mm, buccal 1.5 mm above

ans.text: Read in sequence, the teeth rise progressively off the plane from front to back while the palatal side stays lower than the buccal — and that rise IS the compensating curve, anteroposteriorly and mediolaterally.

saqs.q: Define the compensating curve.
saqs.a: THE ANTEROPOSTERIOR CURVING AND THE MEDIOLATERAL CURVING OF THE OCCLUDING SURFACES AND INCISAL EDGES OF ARTIFICIAL TEETH THAT IS USED TO DEVELOP BALANCED ARTICULATION.

ans.text: The anteroposterior and mediolateral curving of the occluding surfaces and incisal edges of artificial teeth, used to develop balanced articulation.

saqs.q: Define Christensen's phenomenon and explain how the compensating curve answers it.
saqs.a: CHRISTENSEN'S PHENOMENON is THE SPACE THAT OCCURS BETWEEN OPPOSING OCCLUSAL SURFACES DURING MANDIBULAR PROTRUSION. As the mandible protrudes the condyles travel down the eminences, the back of the mandible drops, and a wedge-shaped gap opens posteriorly. Curving the posterior occlusal surfaces upwards means the teeth still meet in that position, so the denture stays balanced instead of tipping.

ans.text: The space that occurs between opposing occlusal surfaces during mandibular protrusion.

head: Why the gap opens
How the curve answers it
rows: as the mandible protrudes the condyles travel down the eminences, the back of the mandible drops, and a wedge-shaped gap opens posteriorly
curving the posterior occlusal surfaces upwards means the teeth still meet in that position — so the denture stays balanced instead of tipping

saqs.q: Which tooth is the key tooth in occlusion, when is it set, and what is the key of occlusion?
saqs.a: The MANDIBULAR FIRST MOLAR is the KEY TOOTH IN OCCLUSION, so it is ARRANGED FIRST. The KEY OF OCCLUSION is that the MESIOBUCCAL CUSP OF THE UPPER FIRST MOLAR OCCLUDES WITH THE MESIOBUCCAL GROOVE OF THE LOWER FIRST MOLAR.

rows: the mandibular first molar — so it has to be arranged first
the mesiobuccal cusp of the UPPER first molar occludes with the mesiobuccal groove of the LOWER first molar

saqs.q: Give the setting instruction for each mandibular posterior tooth.
saqs.a: 1st MOLAR — begin here; the MESIAL BUCCAL CUSP TIP engages the EMBRASURE BETWEEN THE 1st MOLAR AND 2nd PREMOLAR. 2nd PREMOLAR — its BUCCAL CUSP occludes with the ADJACENT MARGINAL RIDGES OF THE MAXILLARY 1st AND 2nd PREMOLARS. 1st PREMOLAR — its BUCCAL CUSP engages the MESIAL MARGINAL RIDGE OF THE OPPOSING 1st PREMOLAR. 2nd MOLAR — the MESIOBUCCAL CUSP engages BETWEEN THE MAXILLARY 1st AND 2nd MOLARS and contacts their marginal ridges.

head: Tooth
Setting instruction
rows: the mesial buccal cusp tip engages the embrasure between the 1st molar and 2nd premolar
its buccal cusp occludes with the adjacent marginal ridges of the maxillary 1st and 2nd premolars
its buccal cusp engages the mesial marginal ridge of the opposing 1st premolar
the mesiobuccal cusp engages between the maxillary 1st and 2nd molars and contacts their marginal ridges

saqs.q: State the single principle behind the mandibular posterior set-up, and the check that follows it.
saqs.a: THE MANDIBULAR CUSP TIPS ARE DESIGNED TO ENGAGE THE EMBRASURES OF THE OPPOSING MAXILLARY TEETH. Afterwards, VERIFY THAT THE POSTERIOR MANDIBULAR TEETH ARE CENTERED OVER THE CREST OF THE RIDGE — a tooth set off the crest turns every vertical bite force into a tipping force on a base that only rests on mucosa.

ans.text: The principle — the mandibular cusp tips are designed to engage the embrasures of the opposing maxillary teeth.

The check — verify that the posterior mandibular teeth are centered over the crest of the ridge. A tooth set off the crest turns every vertical bite force into a tipping force on a base that only rests on mucosa.

saqs.q: What relationship holds between centric occlusion and centric relation in complete dentures, and why?
saqs.a: CENTRIC OCCLUSION = CENTRIC RELATION IN COMPLETE DENTURES. They are deliberately made the same because there is no periodontal ligament to accommodate a slide, and any discrepancy would displace the base.

ans.text: Centric occlusion = centric relation in complete dentures. They are deliberately made the same because there is no periodontal ligament to accommodate a slide, and any discrepancy would displace the base.

saqs.q: List the seven differences between natural dentition and denture 'dentition'.
saqs.a: (1) Natural: retained in the PDL — Denture: MOBILE BASES ON MUCOSA. (2) Natural: teeth move INDEPENDENTLY — Denture: AS A UNIT. (3) Natural: malocclusion effects NOT immediate — Denture: affects the ENTIRE BASE IMMEDIATELY. (4) Natural: non-vertical forces affect ONLY the teeth involved and are WELL TOLERATED — Denture: affect ALL teeth and are TRAUMATIC. (5) Natural: incising DOESN'T affect the posteriors — Denture: affects ALL TEETH ATTACHED TO THE BASE. (6) Natural: bilateral balance is RARE — Denture: OFTEN DESIRED, for BASE STABILITY. (7) Natural: TACTILE SENSITIVITY — Denture: DECREASED TACTILE SENSE.

head: NATURAL dentition
DENTURE 'dentition'
rows: affect only the teeth involved, usually well tolerated
affects all teeth attached to the base

saqs.q: Why do so many of the denture/natural differences come down to the same underlying fact?
saqs.a: Because the denture is ONE RIGID UNIT RESTING ON MUCOSA. A force anywhere on it is a force everywhere on it, and the mucosa — unlike the periodontal ligament — is not built to receive it. That single fact explains why malocclusion affects the whole base immediately, why non-vertical forces are traumatic, why incising loads the posteriors, and why bilateral balance is needed for stability.

ans.text: Because the denture is one rigid unit resting on mucosa. A force anywhere on it is a force everywhere on it, and the mucosa — unlike the periodontal ligament — is not built to receive it.

saqs.q: Distinguish occlusion from articulation.
saqs.a: OCCLUSION is the STATIC relationship between the incising or masticating surfaces of the maxillary or mandibular teeth. ARTICULATION is the STATIC AND DYNAMIC contact relationship between the occlusal surfaces DURING FUNCTION. Articulation includes the movement — which is why the goal of the set-up is called balanced ARTICULATION, not balanced occlusion.

head: OCCLUSION
ARTICULATION
rows: the STATIC relationship between the incising or masticating surfaces of the maxillary or mandibular teeth
the STATIC AND DYNAMIC contact relationship between the occlusal surfaces during function

ans.text: Articulation includes the movement — which is why the goal of the set-up is called balanced articulation, not balanced occlusion.

saqs.q: Define balanced articulation and unpack its four requirements.
saqs.a: THE BILATERAL, SIMULTANEOUS ANTERIOR AND POSTERIOR OCCLUSAL CONTACT OF TEETH IN CENTRIC AND ECCENTRIC POSITIONS. The contact must be BILATERAL (both sides), SIMULTANEOUS (at the same instant), ANTERIOR AND POSTERIOR (front and back), and present in CENTRIC AND ECCENTRIC positions (at rest and in every excursion). Its purpose is STABILITY.

ans.text: The bilateral, simultaneous anterior and posterior occlusal contact of teeth in centric and eccentric positions.

saqs.q: In which four positions must a denture set-up balance?
saqs.a: CENTRIC, PROTRUSIVE, and on the WORKING and NON-WORKING (BALANCING) sides in lateral excursion. With anatomic posterior teeth the aim is BILATERAL POSTERIOR CENTRIC CONTACT, CENTRALIZED FORCES and a BALANCED occlusion TO MINIMIZE TIPPING.

ans.text: With anatomic posterior teeth the aim is bilateral posterior centric contact, centralized forces and a balanced occlusion to minimize tipping.

saqs.q: List the five factors affecting occlusal balance.
saqs.a: (1) CONDYLAR GUIDANCE. (2) INCISAL GUIDANCE. (3) ORIENTATION OF THE OCCLUSAL PLANE. (4) COMPENSATING CURVE. (5) CUSPAL INCLINATION.

saqs.q: What is condylar guidance, and what is special about it among the five factors?
saqs.a: CONDYLAR GUIDANCE IS DUE TO THE PATH THE CONDYLES FOLLOW IN THE TMJ. Of the five factors, THE PATIENT PRESENTS YOU WITH CONDYLAR GUIDANCE — it is fixed and patient-determined. The other four are under the operator's control, and are adjusted to achieve balance with whatever condylar guidance the patient happens to have.

ans.text: Condylar guidance is due to the path the condyles follow in the TMJ.

head: CONDYLAR GUIDANCE
The other four factors
rows: the patient presents you with it — it is fixed and patient-determined
under the operator's control, and adjusted to achieve balance with whatever condylar guidance the patient happens to have

saqs.q: Give the three types of posterior tooth by cuspal inclination, and say how the choice affects the rest of the set-up.
saqs.a: 33 degrees = ANATOMIC, 20 degrees = SEMI-ANATOMIC, 0 degrees = NON-ANATOMIC. The steeper the cusp selected, the more faithfully the other four factors must be set for balance to be achieved; a 0-degree tooth has no cusp to interfere, so it forgives inaccuracy at the cost of cutting efficiency and appearance.

ans.text: The steeper the cusp selected, the more faithfully the other four factors must be set for balance to be achieved. A 0-degree tooth has no cusp to interfere, so it forgives inaccuracy — at the cost of cutting efficiency and appearance.

saqs.q: Define festoon.
saqs.a: CARVINGS IN THE DENTURE BASE MATERIAL OF A DENTURE THAT SIMULATE THE CONTOURS OF THE NATURAL TISSUES BEING REPLACED — the marginal gingiva, interdental gingiva, attached gingiva, root eminences and frena.

ans.text: Carvings in the denture base material that simulate the contours of the natural tissues being replaced by the denture.

saqs.q: Set out the clinical and laboratory procedures of patient visit 4.
saqs.a: CLINICAL — the TRY-IN APPOINTMENT. LABORATORY — FLASKING, DEFLASKING, LABORATORY REMOUNT, and FINISHING AND POLISHING. The try-in is where the completed arrangement is tested in the patient's mouth for esthetics, phonetics and occlusion before it is ever processed in acrylic.

ans.text: The try-in is where the completed arrangement is tested in the patient's mouth for esthetics, phonetics and occlusion — before it is ever processed in acrylic.
